extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, data analysts, journalists and policy researchers using audience/circulation data
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, definitions, selection rules and caveats used by Pew Research Center to assemble and vet circulation and digital audience metrics (comScore, AAM, publisher statements) for the State of the News Media fact sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting digital copies from all-access programs
rubrics_metrics.description: AAM began counting digital copies from all-access programs as single copy sales (under a test period agreed to by publishers and advertisers). These copies were only counted if a reader paid for the program and then requested or “favorited” a specific magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This counting practice applied to 2014 data under test conditions and was to be measured differently starting with 2016 data; changes in distribution plans or app compliance with AAM rules can materially affect counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital issue circulation (AAM 'digital issue' category)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'digital issue' circulation category includes copies that typically feature the same advertising and editorial content as the print edition, although the content may be augmented with hyperlinks or additional media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category is included in AAM publisher statements and was the basis for reported news magazine digital circulation figures in the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital nonreplica circulation
rubrics_metrics.description: AAM's 'digital nonreplica' circulation generally represents editorial and advertising served on paywalled sites and apps and has been shortened or fundamentally altered to better suit the digital platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Pew sample only The Economist and The Nation reported digital nonreplica circulation; treat nonreplica counts as conceptually different from replica 'digital issue' counts when comparing circulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-access program revenue-sharing model
rubrics_metrics.description: All-access services (e.g., Texture, Readly, Magzter Gold) generally share revenue with publishers based on the amount of time users spent with each publisher’s content or the amount of content consumed; Magzter Gold also incorporates magazines’ subscription prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rise of these services can increase reach and revenue but also risk subscriber cannibalization; the revenue impact was considered unclear given the newness of the programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: App-subscription counting caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed changes in digital subscription counts may be due in part to how app subscribers are counted (changes in counting methodology or app compliance with auditing rules can alter reported figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting year-over-year subscription trends, analysts should account for possible measurement artifacts from counting rules or app updates that affect inclusion in audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: comScore entity vetting and removal of non-trendable entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers worked directly with comScore to identify and remove from the sample web entities whose traffic shifts over time were the result of changes in how those entities are measured by comScore, rather than organic changes in audience behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities judged to have 'non-trendable' data (measurement or site-structure-driven shifts) were excluded from trend analyses; researchers consulted comScore analysts throughout the entity selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use total-domain entities when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: For all outlets, entities that are representative of an entire web domain ('total domain entities') were used whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When domain entities were incomplete, custom entities that represent the total domain were used when available; multiple entities of the same URL that resulted from a comScore structure change were considered comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large loss or gain threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A large loss or gain represents at least a 10% difference between 2014 and 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This threshold was used to classify substantial year-over-year changes in unique visitors or minutes per visit in the presented charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Digital Population definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Total Digital Population is the unduplicated combination of the desktop (web browsing + video) and mobile traffic figures (websites and associated apps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use unduplicated cross-platform measures to avoid double-counting users when aggregating desktop and mobile audience figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traffic-volume threshold for candidate selection (comScore categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers assessed all domains from 11 comScore categories with at least 10 million average monthly unique digital visitors in the fourth quarter of 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From domains meeting this 10 million threshold, analysts then selected digital-native news websites using the additional editorial criteria listed for digital-native publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital-native publisher criterion: born on the web
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be 'born on the web,' i.e., not the website of a legacy news brand (note: may be owned by a legacy media company).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being born on the web was a necessary condition for inclusion in the 'digital-native' sample, but ownership by legacy firms did not automatically exclude an entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital-native publisher criterion: original news content
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a publisher of original content about news, defined as current events affecting public life; judged by an assessment of the material appearing on their home page (evidence such as interviews, eyewitness accounts or referral to source documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A review of top stories on the home page should render some evidence of original reporting by a dedicated reportorial/editorial staff; self-description as a news/journalism organization could also be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital-native publisher criterion: not primarily focused on reviews/advice/data
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not entirely focused on reviews, advice, recipes or unedited raw data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites devoted principally to lifestyle how-to content, recipes, or raw data without reporting were excluded from the 'digital-native news' set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital-native publisher criterion: not user-generated/aggregated
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not primarily a user-generated or aggregated content platform (such as Medium, Reddit or Wikipedia); branded content (e.g., NBA.com) was also excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites must produce or commission editorial reporting rather than function mainly as aggregation or user-posting platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of authoritative external lists for specialized sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no official census exists (e.g., black-focused digital news media), researchers relied on established external lists (e.g., Maynard Institute) and matched those lists to comScore total-domain entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities on external lists that lacked trendable data were excluded; use recognized community/industry lists to identify sector participants when no single registry exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concordant-entity reporting rule for multi-entity organizations (cable example)
rubrics_metrics.description: For cable networks, researchers used both the total-domain entity for each network and the entity representing the parent organization; only statements true for both entities were made about each network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple comScore entities represent different aspects of the same organization, restrict claims to items that hold across all relevant entities to avoid overstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and conflict-explanation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: All sources are cited in footnotes or within the narrative and in all graphics; where data conflicted the Center included all relevant sources and tried to explain their differences in footnotes or the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aggregating multiple datasets, document sources and transparently describe contradictions or methodological differences rather than selecting one unannotated figure.
